::: {.callout-tip title="Where you are: Level 1"}
This website is **Level 1 — Foundations**: the whole 8-session course, from a clinical question to a draft manuscript. Level 2 and Level 3 are separate courses that build on it.
:::

![](images/figures/common/two_levels.png){fig-alt="Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3"}

- **Level 1 — Foundations (this course).** Understand research from question to publication. A whole department, no software; the analyses are demonstrated live on FLUID-ICU.
- **Level 2 — Doing the analysis (in preparation).** A separate hands-on course in R for an interested subgroup who want to run, check and report the analyses themselves.
- **Level 3 — Advanced topics (on request).** Specialised methods for complex designs and data, as workshops or consultancy on the participant's own project.

📥 [Course levels overview (PDF)](files/docs/Course_Levels_Overview.pdf)

**Organisation:** Neudata — *#ClearDataClearImpact*

Neudata's clinical-research training runs in three levels. Each level builds on the one before, and each department can stop at the level that fits its needs.

| | **Level 1 — Foundations** | **Level 2 — Doing the analysis** | **Level 3 — Advanced topics** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **In one line** | Understand research from question to publication | Do the analysis yourself, properly, in R | Tackle complex designs and data with Neudata |
| **Who** | A whole department (~30 doctors, nurses, pharmacists) | An interested subgroup (8–12) who want to run their own analyses | Researchers with a specific complex project or dataset |
| **Prerequisites** | None | Level 1 + the free Neudata course *Clinical Data Analysis in R* (or equivalent basics) | Level 2 (or equivalent experience), plus a real question or dataset |
| **Format** | 8 × 3 h over 4 weekends | 8 × 3 h over about 4–6 weeks, with homework | Workshops of 1–2 sessions, or consultancy, on request |
| **Software** | None for participants (instructor demos) | R and RStudio on own laptops | R (and specialised packages) |
| **Hands-on?** | Concepts, reading and interpreting; analyses demonstrated live on FLUID-ICU | Every session is hands-on coding | Hands-on on the participant's own data |
| **Outcome** | A group research proposal and a group draft manuscript | A reproducible analysis and a draft Results section, on own or course data | A completed analysis plan or analysis for a real project, with Neudata support |
| **Documents** | [This website](index.qmd) (the full Level 1 course) | [Level 2](level2.qmd) | [Level 3](level3.qmd) |

## How the levels connect

- **Level 1 → Level 2.** In Level 1, participants *read* the FLUID-ICU analyses (Table 1, crude vs adjusted ORs, Kaplan–Meier, multiple imputation) that the instructor runs. In Level 2 they **run, check and report those same analyses themselves**, then apply them to their own data. The FLUID-ICU dataset and R scripts in `Course/Data/` are shared by both levels.
- **Level 2 → Level 3.** Level 2 makes participants confident with descriptive statistics, linear and logistic regression, missing data and reproducible reporting. Level 3 takes the methods that real clinical data often demand — meta-analysis, prediction models, diagnostic accuracy, advanced survival analysis, longitudinal and multilevel models, large or clustered datasets — and works on them with the participant's own project.

## Progression at a glance

| Skill | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Research question, design, ethics | Taught in depth | Assumed | Assumed |
| Data management and cleaning | Concepts; live demo | Hands-on: import, clean, validate, cleaning log, data dictionary, version control | Large, linked or clustered data |
| Describing data, Table 1, figures | Read and judge | Build publication-ready tables and figures | Specialised plots (forest, funnel, calibration, cumulative incidence) |
| Regression | Read and interpret outputs | Fit, check, interpret and report linear and logistic models | Mixed models, competing risks, time-varying covariates, prediction models |
| Missing data | Mechanisms and ideas | Complete-case vs multiple imputation (mice) in practice | Complex imputation (multilevel, longitudinal) |
| Survival analysis | Read Kaplan–Meier and HRs | Intro only (via FLUID-ICU scripts) | In depth |
| Writing and publishing | Full manuscript workflow (group draft) | Reproducible report → Results section | Methods and results for complex analyses |

**Status:** Level 1 materials are in `Course/`. Level 2 and Level 3 are outlines — materials to be developed after Level 1 has run.
